SDI-12 Manager

Discover, address, configure and test SDI-12 sensors on the logger via serial passthrough. The output window below shows raw replies for verification.

Serial passthrough

Status—

SDI-12 access uses the device's serial passthrough; behaviour depends on the logger firmware and wiring. The output window shows raw replies for verification.

Discovered sensors

Scan to discover SDI-12 sensors.

Raw SDI-12 command

Every SDI-12 command ends with !. The leading z (LTX serial bridge) is added automatically. Use ? as the wildcard address. Address chars: 0-9 a-z A-Z.

SDI-12 Smart

Finds, reads, names and adds your SDI-12 sensors — step by step.

Set up your sensors

SDI-12 is a simple wiring standard that lets the logger talk to digital sensors. Press the button: the app powers the bus, checks the addresses and lists every sensor it finds — ready to name, measure and add.

Advanced: SDI-12 bus setup (commands)

After "Add to logger" the logger may still read "NoValue" until the SDI-12 bus device itself is configured (just like the Modbus z?XK/z?XC/z?XU/z?XP/z?XWrite setup). Paste the manufacturer's command sequence here; each line is sent over the logger's z-bridge and the device replies are logged below. The exact SDI-12 syntax is firmware-specific — get it from GeoPrecision/joembedded.

Help & FAQ

What is SDI-12?

SDI-12 is a common 3-wire standard for connecting digital environmental sensors (water level, soil moisture, temperature…) to a data logger. Each sensor sits on the same bus and answers when called by its address.

What is an address?

Every sensor on the bus has a one-character address (usually 0–9). It is how the logger tells two sensors apart. If two sensors share an address they clash — this assistant warns you and lets you change one.

How do I add a sensor to the logger?

First press Measure so the assistant knows how many values the sensor delivers, then press “Add to logger”. It prepares one logger channel per value and opens the Parameters page so you can review and write them.

Radio 433 MHz — value mapping

Wireless sensors transmit measurements on 433 MHz. An SDI-12 radio adapter on the logger collects those values and exposes them as SDI-12 D-values. Here you read those collected values and map each one to a logger channel — comfortably and reproducibly.

Radio adapter (SDI-12)

Status—

The wireless SDI-12 dongle is reached over the LTX z serial bridge. List wireless nodes sends z*15000 ?XL! (the manufacturer's scan433sdi.crun command, 15 s) to enumerate the 433 MHz nodes the dongle has collected; the raw reply appears in the log below. Use ? as the wildcard address. The exact ?XL! reply layout is dongle-firmware specific.

Advanced: dongle node configuration (XP)

Assigns 433 MHz node IDs to the dongle's slots, exactly like the manufacturer's work.crun. Each z…XP<n>=…! line is sent verbatim over the z-bridge, bracketed by z+/z-. Edit the node IDs (6-hex) to match your sensors. Format is dongle-firmware specific — values shown are the manufacturer's example.

Found wireless nodes 0

Select a node found by the dongle scan to keep working with it: create channel mappings from its values, or insert it into the dongle's node configuration.

No nodes yet. Press “List wireless nodes (?XL!)” above to scan the 433 MHz band.

Selected node: —

—

“Generate & send converter configuration” builds the z…XP<n>=…! command list for all listed nodes (each needs a 4-hex PIN), writes it into the configuration above for review, then press Send node config to program the converter.

To combine several loggers: program the first node, scan again for the next one, then use Add this node to the configuration — its XP lines are appended with continued slot numbers so both loggers' values are read. Then press Send node config.

Collected radio values

Read the adapter to list its collected 433 MHz values.

Add a mapping manually

Mappings persist per logger (by device address). Use “Assign to logger channels” to write them into the parameter set.

Funkadapter SDI-12 Smart

Register your 433-MHz wireless loggers on the SDI-12 radio converter by simply typing each logger's ID and PIN. Add as many nodes as you like, then transfer everything to the converter with one click. Afterwards the loggers' values appear as SDI-12 channels in “SDI-12 Smart” / “SDI-12 Manager”.

1Radio converter Converter address: —

First press “Identify converter” so the app learns the converter's SDI-12 address. The configuration is sent to exactly this address — the converter's address is never changed.

2Your wireless loggers

For each logger, type its Logger-ID (SNO, 6 hex — e.g. A54366) and PIN / access code (4 hex — e.g. F9D0) from the device label, and how many channels it has (default 1).
